literal: Even if the wealth that yields good is great, to the noble, the wealth obtained by killing is the lowest.
translation: Even if the wealth that brings goodness is immensely great, to the virtuous, wealth obtained by killing other living beings is utterly base.
modern: நன்மையைத் தரும் செல்வம் மிகப் பெரியதாக இருந்தாலும், பிற உயிர்களைக் கொல்வதன் மூலம் கிடைக்கும் செல்வம் சான்றோர்களுக்கு மிக இழிவானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the absolute commitment of virtuous people to the principle of non-killing. Even if a particular gain or wealth ('ஆக்கம்') is incredibly vast ('பெரிது') and promises great benefits ('நன்றாகும்'), it is deemed utterly base ('கடை') by the noble ('சான்றோர்') if it is acquired by destroying life ('கொன்று'). For the truly wise, no amount of material prosperity can justify the act of killing. The contrast between the greatness of the gain and its moral lowliness emphasizes that ethical purity always triumphs over material success.
